section_title: What happens when Jerusalem must drink her sister’s cup?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 22 Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will incite your lovers against you, those from whom you turned away in disgust. And I will bring them against you from every side— 23 the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, the men of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them—all desirable young men, governors and commanders, officers and men of renown, mounted on horses. 24 They will come against you with a host of peoples, with weapons, chariots, and wagons. They will array themselves against you on every side with buckler and shield and helmet. I will delegate judgment to them, and they will punish you according to their own standards. 25 And I will set My jealous rage against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your noses and ears, and your survivors will fall by the sword. They will seize your sons and daughters, and your remnant will be consumed by fire. 26 They will strip off your clothes and take your fine jewelry. 27 So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt, and you will not lift your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.’

28 For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Surely I will deliver you into the hands of those you hate, from whom you turned away in disgust. 29 They will treat you with hatred, take all for which you have worked, and leave you naked and bare, so that the shame of your prostitution will be exposed. Your indecency and promiscuity 30 have brought these things upon you, because you have prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols. 31 Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.’

32 This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You will drink your sister’s cup, a cup deep and wide. It will bring scorn and derision, for it holds so much. 33 You will be filled with drunkenness and grief, with a cup of devastation and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria. 34 You will drink it and drain it; you will dash it to pieces, and tear your breasts. For I have spoken,’ declares the Lord GOD. 35 Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your indecency and prostitution.’”

context_lines: The Lord announces that the former lovers Jerusalem now hates will gather against her. The impressive armies that once attracted her will surround the city and become its enemies.

The threatened losses are severe: mutilation, death, captivity, fire, and the stripping away of clothing and jewelry. The story’s marriage language becomes a picture of the city losing its people, possessions and security.

The cup gathers the warning into one image. Jerusalem will drink the devastation and grief Samaria has already experienced. The final charge explains the relationship behind all of this: she has forgotten the Lord and cast Him behind her back.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/23.htm) understands the cup as the sorrow and punishment Jerusalem must endure. The [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/ezekiel/23) connect it with the wider biblical picture of a cup of divine punishment. The sister’s experience makes the warning concrete: Jerusalem cannot assume she will escape the path she has chosen.
The announced judgment belongs to the Lord’s confrontation with these cities. The passage does not give people permission to mutilate or attack an unfaithful spouse.
god_plan_lines: The cup becomes a powerful picture again when Jesus faces His suffering. In [Mark 14:32–42](https://biblehub.com/bsb/mark/14.htm), He asks that the cup might pass from Him, yet submits to the Father’s will. In [John 18:1–11](https://biblehub.com/bsb/john/18.htm), He refuses Peter’s attempt to prevent His arrest and accepts the cup the Father has given Him.

This is a connection in the wider biblical theme, not a statement that Ezekiel’s cup directly predicts Jesus. Jerusalem is facing the consequences of its own unfaithfulness; Jesus willingly goes toward the suffering through which He offers Himself for sins. [Hebrews 10:10–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/hebrews/10.htm) explains the lasting result of His one offering: forgiveness that removes the need for another offering for sin.
